item.content:encoded:
If you are a student or recent graduate looking for internship opportunities with a major international airline, Southwest Airlines is inviting prospective candidates to learn more about its 2027 internship opportunities through upcoming virtual Campus Reach information sessions.

The sessions are designed to give students an opportunity to connect with the Southwest Airlines Campus Reach recruiting team and learn more about internship opportunities available for the 2027 program cycle. Two online sessions are scheduled for Monday, August 31, 2026, giving interested participants the flexibility to choose between two different times.

In addition to the internship information sessions, Southwest Airlines will participate in the Latino Professionals in Aerospace (LPA) Annual Conference 2026 in Orlando, Florida, from September 17–18, 2026.

For students seeking professional experience, exposure to a major airline employer, and information about future internship recruitment, these events provide an opportunity to learn directly from Southwest Airlines’ recruiting team.

Opportunity Category

Category: Internship / Career Recruitment Information Event

The Campus Reach sessions are not themselves internship placements. They are virtual information and recruitment sessions designed to showcase Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internship opportunities and help prospective candidates understand the opportunities and recruitment process.

The LPA Annual Conference is a separate professional career event where Southwest Airlines’ recruiting teams will be present.

About Southwest Airlines

Southwest Airlines is a major U.S. airline and employer with a large workforce and a wide range of career opportunities across aviation, technology, business, operations, communications, marketing, finance, customer experience, engineering, and other professional areas.

The airline’s Campus Reach initiative focuses on engaging students and early-career professionals and introducing them to opportunities available within the organization.

For students interested in entering the aviation and corporate sectors, attending an employer information session can be valuable because it allows candidates to understand the organization before submitting an internship application.

Southwest Airlines 2027 Internship Information Sessions

Southwest Airlines has announced two editions of its Campus Reach: General Internship Information Session on August 31, 2026.

Both sessions cover the same general purpose: introducing students to Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internship opportunities.

Option 1: August 31, 2026

The first virtual session is scheduled for:

  • Date: Monday, August 31, 2026
  • Time: 12:00 p.m. Central Time (CT)
  • Format: Online
  • Event: Campus Reach: General Internship Information Session – Option 1
  • Focus: Southwest Airlines 2027 internship opportunities

Interested students can access the event through the official Southwest Airlines careers website.

Option 2: August 31, 2026

A second session is also scheduled for the same day:

  • Date: Monday, August 31, 2026
  • Time: 5:00 p.m. Central Time (CT)
  • Format: Online
  • Event: Campus Reach: General Internship Information Session – Option 2
  • Focus: Southwest Airlines 2027 internship opportunities

Having two sessions on the same day provides prospective candidates with an alternative time to participate.

Why Attend the Southwest Airlines Internship Information Session?

Attending an employer information session can be useful even before applying for an internship. Instead of submitting an application without knowing much about the employer, students can use the session to understand what the company is looking for and how its internship program works.

1. Learn About 2027 Internship Opportunities

The primary purpose of the sessions is to showcase Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internship opportunities.

Students can use the event as an opportunity to learn about potential positions, areas of work, recruitment timelines, and the broader internship experience.

2. Understand the Recruitment Process

One of the most important advantages of attending an employer-led information session is gaining a better understanding of how recruitment works.

Candidates can use the information provided during the event to prepare for subsequent applications and recruitment stages.

3. Connect With the Campus Reach Team

The sessions are hosted by Southwest Airlines’ Campus Reach Team.

This gives students an opportunity to learn directly from the people involved in student and early-career recruitment rather than relying solely on information found in job advertisements.

4. Discover Career Possibilities Beyond Traditional Aviation Roles

An airline is more than pilots and flight attendants. A large organization such as Southwest Airlines can have career opportunities across numerous professional functions.

Depending on the internship positions available for the 2027 cycle, students may find opportunities connected to areas such as:

  • Communications
  • Marketing
  • Digital media
  • Technology
  • Business
  • Finance
  • Human resources
  • Data and analytics
  • Customer experience
  • Operations
  • Engineering
  • Corporate services
  • Other specialized professional functions

Students should review the official internship listings for the specific positions available when applications open.

5. Prepare Earlier for Internship Recruitment

Internship recruitment can be competitive, particularly for well-known employers.

Participating in an information session before or during the recruitment period can help candidates understand the employer’s expectations and prepare their applications more effectively.

Southwest Airlines and the Latino Professionals in Aerospace Annual Conference 2026

Southwest Airlines is also scheduled to attend the Latino Professionals in Aerospace (LPA) Annual Conference 2026.

The event is scheduled to take place in Orlando, Florida, from September 17 to September 18, 2026.

According to the event information provided by Southwest Airlines, its recruiting teams will attend the conference to engage with participants and share information about careers with the airline.

The conference represents another opportunity for professionals and students interested in aerospace and aviation careers to interact with Southwest Airlines recruiters.

LPA Annual Conference 2026 Details

Key information includes:

  • Event: Latino Professionals in Aerospace Annual Conference 2026
  • Dates: September 17–18, 2026
  • Location: Orlando, Florida, United States
  • Southwest Airlines participation: Recruiting teams
  • Purpose: Career engagement and recruitment
  • Sector: Aviation and aerospace

Those planning to attend the conference should consult the official conference organizers for registration requirements, eligibility, fees, venue information, and other event-specific details.

Who Can Benefit From These Opportunities?

The Campus Reach internship information sessions are primarily relevant to students and prospective early-career candidates interested in Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internship opportunities.

The information provided does not establish a single academic discipline or degree requirement for everyone who attends the information session. Internship eligibility may vary depending on the specific position.

Students should therefore avoid assuming that one qualification applies to every 2027 internship.

Instead, applicants should examine individual internship vacancies for requirements such as:

  • Academic level
  • Degree or field of study
  • Graduation date
  • Technical or professional skills
  • Previous experience
  • Work authorization
  • Location requirements
  • Availability
  • Any position-specific qualifications

International Applicants and Geographic Eligibility

An important distinction should be made between attending the online information session and qualifying for an individual Southwest Airlines internship.

The event listing provided does not state that the virtual information session is restricted by race or nationality.

However, attending an information session does not automatically establish eligibility for employment or an internship.

Southwest Airlines’ internship positions may have specific requirements concerning location, employment eligibility, and authorization to work in the United States. International students should therefore carefully review the requirements attached to each individual internship position.

The information supplied for these events does not identify a specific racial restriction or nationality-based eligibility category for the Campus Reach information sessions.

Southwest Airlines also states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer and that employment decisions are made without regard to various legally protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, military or veteran status, disability, and genetic information.

Important Dates

Applicants and prospective candidates should keep the following dates in mind:

Event Date Format/Location
Campus Reach Internship Information Session – Option 1 August 31, 2026, 12:00 p.m. CT Online
Campus Reach Internship Information Session – Option 2 August 31, 2026, 5:00 p.m. CT Online
Latino Professionals in Aerospace Annual Conference September 17–18, 2026 Orlando, Florida

Deadline

There is no application deadline stated in the provided event information for the Campus Reach information sessions.

The key date for students interested in attending the virtual internship sessions is August 31, 2026.

For the LPA Annual Conference, the provided information lists the event dates as September 17–18, 2026, but does not provide a separate registration deadline.

Candidates should therefore check the relevant official event pages for registration availability and any updated deadlines.

How to Prepare for the Southwest Airlines Internship Opportunity

Simply attending an information session is only one part of preparing for a competitive internship application.

Students can take several steps before the event.

1. Update Your Resume

Make sure your resume clearly communicates your academic background, skills, projects, leadership experience, volunteer activities, employment history, and relevant achievements.

Keep the document easy to read and focus on measurable accomplishments where possible.

For example, instead of simply writing:

Managed social media.

A stronger description could explain the scope and result:

Created and managed social media campaigns that increased audience engagement and improved digital reach.

2. Research Southwest Airlines

Before attending the session, learn about the company, its business operations, values, career areas, and internship opportunities.

Research allows you to ask more meaningful questions and demonstrates genuine interest.

3. Prepare Questions

Do not attend an employer information session passively.

Prepare questions in advance. Useful questions could include:

  • What does Southwest Airlines look for in successful internship candidates?
  • What academic backgrounds are commonly represented among interns?
  • What is the typical internship recruitment timeline?
  • What skills make an internship application stand out?
  • Are interns given opportunities to work on real projects?
  • What opportunities exist for interns after completing their internships?
  • How can students prepare for the interview process?
  • When will the 2027 internship vacancies be posted?

4. Review Your LinkedIn Profile

Recruiters may look at candidates’ professional profiles.

Make sure your LinkedIn profile contains:

  • A professional headline
  • Updated education information
  • Relevant experience
  • Skills
  • Projects
  • Certifications
  • Professional achievements
  • A professional profile photograph

5. Prepare a Short Introduction

If interaction with recruiters is available, prepare a concise introduction about yourself.

A good introduction should communicate:

  1. Who you are
  2. What you are studying or your professional background
  3. Your area of interest
  4. Why you are interested in Southwest Airlines
  5. What type of internship you are seeking

For example:

“I am a communication studies graduate with experience in digital marketing, corporate communications, content creation, and social media management. I am particularly interested in opportunities that combine communications, digital engagement, and business strategy. I am interested in learning more about Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internship opportunities and how candidates with communications and digital skills can contribute.”

Why Internship Information Sessions Matter

Students sometimes overlook employer information sessions because they do not immediately provide an internship offer.

However, these events can play an important role in the recruitment process.

An information session can help candidates:

  • Understand an employer’s expectations
  • Learn about upcoming vacancies
  • Discover career areas they had not previously considered
  • Prepare better applications
  • Understand recruitment timelines
  • Learn how to position their skills
  • Identify questions to ask recruiters
  • Become familiar with the employer’s culture and opportunities

For competitive internship programs, preparation before an application can be just as important as submitting the application itself.

Southwest Airlines Talent Community

The information provided by Southwest Airlines also encourages people who do not find their desired position immediately to join its Talent Community.

Joining a talent community can be useful for candidates who want to receive updates about future employment opportunities.

Rather than waiting until the exact position you want appears, joining an employer’s talent network can help you stay informed about new opportunities.

Candidates should still monitor official vacancy announcements because joining a talent community does not necessarily constitute an application for a specific job or internship.

Equal Opportunity and Accessibility

Southwest Airlines states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fair hiring practices.

The company indicates that employment decisions are made without regard to legally protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, military or veteran status, disability, and genetic information.

The company also provides information for candidates who require accessibility accommodations during the online careers or hiring process.

Applicants who need an accommodation should follow the instructions provided on the official Southwest Airlines careers platform.

Important Considerations for International Students

International students should pay particular attention to eligibility requirements when reviewing Southwest Airlines internships.

The fact that an online information session can be accessed remotely does not necessarily mean that every internship is open to candidates worldwide.

Individual internship positions may have specific requirements related to:

  • U.S. work authorization
  • Internship location
  • Student status
  • Graduation dates
  • Academic programs
  • Employment eligibility
  • Other position-specific conditions

Therefore, international applicants should carefully read the eligibility requirements for each internship before investing time in the application process.

How to Find the Internship Opportunities

Interested candidates should use the official Southwest Airlines careers platform to locate current internship vacancies and event information.

When searching, candidates should look for:

  • 2027 internship positions
  • Campus Reach opportunities
  • Student opportunities
  • Early-career opportunities
  • Position-specific qualifications
  • Application deadlines
  • Location requirements
  • Work authorization requirements

Candidates should rely on official Southwest Airlines recruitment information rather than unofficial job reposting websites whenever possible.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Southwest Airlines 2027 Internship Opportunities

Final Thoughts

Southwest Airlines’ upcoming Campus Reach information sessions provide students and early-career candidates with an opportunity to learn more about the airline’s 2027 internship opportunities directly from its recruiting team.

With two virtual sessions scheduled for August 31, 2026, candidates can choose between the 12:00 p.m. CT and 5:00 p.m. CT sessions. The airline will also participate in the Latino Professionals in Aerospace Annual Conference 2026 in Orlando, Florida, on September 17–18, 2026, creating another opportunity for career-focused engagement with Southwest Airlines recruiters.

The information sessions should not be viewed as a guarantee of an internship placement. Instead, they are an opportunity to gain useful information, understand the recruitment process, prepare strategically, and learn about the range of opportunities available within a major airline.

Candidates interested in Southwest Airlines’ 2027 internships should begin preparing their resumes, researching the organization, reviewing available positions, checking eligibility requirements, and preparing thoughtful questions before attending.

For international candidates, including applicants from Africa and other regions outside the United States, the most important step is to review the eligibility and work-authorization requirements attached to each individual internship position. Geographic accessibility to an online event should not be confused with eligibility for employment.

Ultimately, early preparation can give prospective applicants a significant advantage. By attending the information session, researching the organization, preparing a strong application, and monitoring official internship announcements, students can position themselves more effectively for the 2027 Southwest Airlines internship recruitment cycle.

item.content:encoded:
The World Future Council (WFC) has opened nominations for the World Future Policy Award (WFPA) 2027, focusing on Education for Sustainable Development in Cities. The prestigious global policy award seeks outstanding laws, policies, provisions and frameworks that use education, lifelong learning and community participation to help cities become more inclusive, sustainable, resilient and peaceful.

Unlike awards that primarily recognise individual personalities, the World Future Policy Award focuses on exemplary policy solutions that can inspire governments, communities and decision-makers around the world. The 2027 edition is particularly interested in policies that demonstrate how cities and communities can empower people of different ages and backgrounds to participate meaningfully in sustainable urban development.

The call is open to nominations from a broad range of organisations and stakeholders, including international organisations, governments, government agencies, parliaments, academia, non-governmental organisations, Indigenous communities, local communities and other relevant actors. Policies may operate at national, regional, subnational or local levels.

Nomination deadline: 31 October 2026.

About the World Future Policy Award 2027

The World Future Policy Award is presented by the World Future Council to raise international awareness of policies that provide effective solutions to major challenges facing present and future generations.

The award aims to identify and showcase policies that are not only effective in their original contexts but also have the potential to inspire action elsewhere. According to the World Future Council, the award’s mission is to raise global awareness of exemplary policies while educating and inspiring policymakers, civil society and the wider public.

For 2027, the award turns its attention to the relationship between education, sustainable development and cities.

This focus recognises that cities are increasingly at the centre of environmental, social, technological and economic transformation. As urban populations grow and societies face increasingly complex challenges, cities need approaches that allow residents to acquire the knowledge, skills and values required to participate in creating sustainable futures.

The World Future Council is therefore looking for policies that demonstrate how education and learning can become an integral part of urban development.

What Is Education for Sustainable Development in Cities?

Education for Sustainable Development, commonly known as ESD, seeks to equip individuals and communities with the knowledge, skills, values and attitudes needed to make informed decisions and contribute to sustainable development.

Within cities, this concept extends beyond traditional classrooms and formal education systems.

It can include:

  • Community-based learning.
  • Lifelong learning programmes.
  • Intergenerational learning.
  • Environmental education.
  • Digital inclusion.
  • Civic education and participation.
  • Skills development for sustainable lifestyles.
  • Community engagement in local decision-making.
  • Learning initiatives supporting climate action.
  • Programmes that promote inclusive and equitable urban development.

The 2027 World Future Policy Award is particularly interested in policies that demonstrate how these approaches can be embedded into the way cities are governed and developed.

The World Future Council notes that cities can create inclusive, lifelong and intergenerational learning opportunities that allow residents to contribute to sustainable, regenerative and just futures.

Why Cities Are Central to Sustainable Development

Cities face many of the world’s most significant development challenges, but they are also important places where solutions can be tested and implemented.

Rapid urbanisation, technological change, environmental pressures and social inequalities are changing the way people live and interact with their communities. These developments create an urgent need for urban populations to have access to learning opportunities that enable them to understand challenges and participate in solutions.

Education can help residents:

  • Understand environmental and climate-related challenges.
  • Adopt more sustainable lifestyles.
  • Participate in local decision-making.
  • Develop digital skills.
  • Engage with public institutions.
  • Understand their rights and responsibilities.
  • Contribute to community development.
  • Support inclusive and peaceful communities.
  • Adapt to technological and economic changes.
  • Build stronger relationships between generations.

The award therefore recognises that sustainable cities cannot be created solely through infrastructure, technology or environmental regulation. People also need opportunities to learn, participate and shape the future of their communities.

Key Areas of Policy the Award Is Looking For

The World Future Council has identified several areas of particular interest for the 2027 award.

1. Greening Cities

The first focus area is policies that support the greening of cities through community-based learning and participation.

This could include policies that help residents understand and participate in:

  • Urban environmental protection.
  • Climate action.
  • Sustainable transportation.
  • Urban agriculture.
  • Biodiversity conservation.
  • Green public spaces.
  • Sustainable waste management.
  • Energy efficiency.
  • Nature-based solutions.
  • Sustainable urban planning.

The strongest nominations are likely to demonstrate how learning and public participation contribute to measurable environmental improvements.

2. Digital Inclusion Strategies

Digital technologies increasingly influence access to education, employment, public services and civic participation.

The award therefore welcomes policies addressing digital inclusion, particularly where such policies help communities overcome barriers to participation.

Relevant policies could involve:

  • Digital literacy.
  • Access to digital learning.
  • Digital skills development.
  • Affordable access to technology.
  • Inclusive digital public services.
  • Digital opportunities for disadvantaged communities.
  • Programmes supporting older people or marginalised groups.
  • Community-based digital education.

A strong policy could demonstrate how digital inclusion allows residents to participate more effectively in sustainable urban development.

3. Civic Participation and Participatory Budgeting

The third highlighted area concerns civic participation, with particular attention to participatory budgeting.

Participatory budgeting gives residents opportunities to participate in decisions concerning the allocation of public resources.

Policies in this area may demonstrate how cities educate and empower residents to:

  • Understand public budgets.
  • Identify community priorities.
  • Participate in decision-making.
  • Propose projects.
  • Deliberate with other community members.
  • Monitor implementation.
  • Hold local institutions accountable.

Such approaches can transform residents from passive recipients of public services into active participants in shaping their communities.

What Makes a Strong Policy Nomination?

The World Future Council has identified several characteristics that it wants to see in nominated policies.

Transformative

The policy should demonstrate meaningful potential to change the way communities address sustainable development.

Innovative

Nominations should showcase creative approaches that provide new or particularly effective ways of connecting education, learning and sustainable urban development.

Inspiring

The policy should provide lessons that can motivate other cities, communities or policymakers to take action.

Inclusive

The World Future Council is particularly interested in approaches that recognise diverse perspectives and ensure that different communities can participate.

Replicable

One of the most important considerations is whether a policy can provide lessons for other places facing similar challenges.

The award specifically encourages nominations of policies that are replicable in similar contexts.

Indigenous and Local Community Policies Are Particularly Welcome

An important feature of the 2027 call is its emphasis on Indigenous and local communities.

The World Future Council is particularly interested in policies that reflect the perspectives, worldviews, cosmologies, cultural traditions and socio-legal perspectives of Indigenous and local communities.

This means that nominations do not have to rely exclusively on conventional government or mainstream educational approaches.

Policies that incorporate locally developed knowledge systems, cultural practices and community perspectives may be particularly relevant when they demonstrate how these approaches contribute to sustainable, inclusive and resilient communities.

What Types of Policies Can Be Nominated?

The World Future Council states that eligible policy instruments can include:

  • Laws.
  • Policies.
  • Provisions.
  • Frameworks.

These can operate at different levels, including:

  • National.
  • Subnational.
  • Regional.
  • Local.

This broad scope means that relevant examples do not necessarily have to be nationwide programmes.

A city policy, municipal framework, regional strategy or community-oriented legal provision may also be relevant if it demonstrates strong connections between education for sustainable development and urban or community development.

Who Can Submit a Nomination?

The call is open to nominations from representatives of a wide range of institutions and organisations.

The World Future Council specifically welcomes nominations from:

  1. International organisations.
  2. Academic institutions and researchers.
  3. Non-governmental organisations.
  4. Parliaments.
  5. Governments.
  6. Government agencies.
  7. Indigenous communities.
  8. Local communities.
  9. Other relevant stakeholders.

This broad approach means that the opportunity is not restricted to government officials or policymakers alone. Organisations and institutions working with communities, education, sustainability, urban development and public policy can also identify and nominate relevant policies.

International Context of the Award

The 2027 focus is connected to broader international commitments concerning education, sustainability and future generations.

The World Future Council highlights the 1997 UNESCO Declaration of the Responsibilities of the Present Generations Toward Future Generations, which emphasises education as a means of promoting peace, justice, tolerance and equality for present and future generations.

The award also connects strongly with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly:

  • SDG 4: Quality Education, which focuses on inclusive and equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all.
  • SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, which focuses on making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable.

Education for Sustainable Development provides an important connection between these two areas by helping communities acquire the knowledge and capabilities needed to participate in sustainable urban transformation.

Partnership Behind the World Future Policy Award 2027

The 2027 World Future Policy Award is being developed with important international partners.

The World Future Council is working together with the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL) and the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU).

The UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning works with UNESCO Member States on lifelong learning, learning ecosystems, skills for life and work, and inclusive learning. The institute also focuses on research, capacity-building, networking and publications relating to lifelong learning.

The Inter-Parliamentary Union is the global organisation of national parliaments and works on areas including democratic governance, human rights, gender equality, youth empowerment, climate action and sustainable development.

This partnership gives the award a strong connection to international policy, lifelong learning, parliamentary engagement and sustainable urban development.

Why This Award Matters

The World Future Policy Award is significant because it focuses on policy solutions rather than individual achievements.

Many cities around the world are experimenting with innovative approaches to sustainability, education and community participation. However, effective local policies can remain relatively unknown outside their immediate communities.

By identifying and showcasing exemplary policies, the award seeks to help successful approaches gain wider international attention.

A recognised policy can potentially provide useful lessons for policymakers in other cities and countries facing similar challenges.

The award therefore serves several purposes:

  • Identifying effective policy solutions.
  • Raising international awareness.
  • Sharing lessons between cities and communities.
  • Encouraging policymakers to take action.
  • Highlighting innovative approaches.
  • Supporting sustainable development.
  • Promoting lifelong learning.
  • Encouraging inclusive civic participation.
  • Amplifying Indigenous and local perspectives.
  • Demonstrating how policy can support future generations.

How to Prepare a Strong Nomination

Anyone considering submitting a nomination should carefully assess whether the policy demonstrates the characteristics sought by the World Future Council.

A strong nomination should clearly explain the policy and its relevance to the award theme.

Consider addressing the following questions:

1. What is the policy?

Clearly identify the law, policy, framework or provision being nominated.

Explain where it operates and which institution or authority is responsible for it.

2. What problem does it address?

Describe the social, environmental, educational or urban challenge that the policy was designed to address.

3. How does education or learning contribute?

Explain how the policy creates opportunities for people to learn, develop skills, participate or exchange knowledge.

4. Who benefits?

Identify the communities, residents, learners, organisations or groups affected by the policy.

5. Is the policy inclusive?

Explain how the policy addresses the needs and perspectives of different groups, including Indigenous and local communities where relevant.

6. What results has it achieved?

Where evidence is available, provide concrete information about outcomes and impact.

This might include improvements in participation, environmental outcomes, digital inclusion, education, community engagement or other measurable areas.

7. Can the approach be replicated?

Explain why the policy could provide useful lessons for other cities or communities.

8. What makes it innovative?

Highlight the elements that distinguish the policy from conventional approaches.

9. How is the policy transformative?

Explain how it has changed systems, institutions, behaviours, participation or community outcomes.

Nomination Deadline

The official nomination deadline for the World Future Policy Award 2027 is: 31 October 2026

Potential nominators should therefore begin preparing their submissions early rather than waiting until the final days of the call.

The World Future Council states that finalists are expected to be announced in May or June 2027. The winning policies will subsequently be celebrated at a high-level award ceremony held jointly with the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning during the International Conference on Learning Cities (ICLC) in 2027.

How to Apply or Submit a Nomination

The process is a nomination, rather than a conventional individual job or scholarship application.

Interested organisations, institutions and stakeholders should first review the official nomination criteria and then complete the nomination form.

The official World Future Council page provides the nomination form as well as translations of the nomination materials in Arabic, French, German, Hindi, Kiswahili, Portuguese and Spanish.

Before submitting, nominators should make sure that the proposed policy clearly relates to Education for Sustainable Development in Cities and demonstrates relevance to one or more of the priority areas.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity World Future Policy Award 2027
Theme Education for Sustainable Development in Cities
Organiser World Future Council
Key partners UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning and Inter-Parliamentary Union
Focus Sustainable development, lifelong learning and urban policy
Eligible nomination Laws, policies, provisions and frameworks
Geographic scope Global
Policy levels National, subnational, regional and local
Key topics Greening cities, digital inclusion and civic participation
Special focus Indigenous and local communities
Nomination deadline 31 October 2026
Finalists announced May or June 2027
Award ceremony International Conference on Learning Cities in 2027

Important Tip for Potential Nominators

Do not focus solely on describing a policy.

A stronger nomination should demonstrate why the policy matters, what it has achieved and why other communities could learn from it.

In particular, nominators should connect the policy to the central idea of empowering people through lifelong and intergenerational learning. The strongest examples are likely to show a clear relationship between learning, community participation and sustainable urban outcomes.

It is also useful to demonstrate evidence of implementation rather than presenting only a theoretical policy proposal. Evidence of community involvement, measurable results, institutional adoption, innovation and potential for replication can make a nomination more compelling.

Visit HERE to learn more about the World Future Policy Award 2027.

Conclusion

The World Future Policy Award 2027: Education for Sustainable Development in Cities provides an important international platform for highlighting policies that place learning, participation and people at the centre of sustainable urban development.

As cities confront rapid urbanisation, environmental pressures, technological change and growing social complexity, education can play a critical role in helping communities understand challenges and participate in building solutions.

The 2027 award is particularly relevant to policies focused on greening cities, digital inclusion and civic participation, including participatory budgeting. It also provides an important opportunity to showcase Indigenous and local approaches that reflect diverse cultural, social and legal perspectives.

Because the award recognises policies rather than simply individuals, it offers governments, municipalities, organisations, academic institutions, Indigenous communities and other stakeholders an opportunity to bring effective policy solutions to international attention.

Organisations and stakeholders with a strong policy example should review the criteria carefully and consider submitting a nomination before the 31 October 2026 deadline. The finalists are expected to be announced in May or June 2027, with the winning policies to be celebrated during the International Conference on Learning Cities in 2027.

For communities working to create more sustainable, inclusive, resilient and peaceful cities, the World Future Policy Award 2027 represents an opportunity to demonstrate how education and lifelong learning can become powerful tools for sustainable urban transformation.

item.content:encoded:
The Defra Research and Development (R&D) Fellowship Programme 2027/28 is now accepting applications from talented scientists, researchers, engineers, and analytical professionals who want to make a real-world impact by contributing to UK government policy. This prestigious fellowship, offered by the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), provides an exceptional opportunity for external researchers from academia and industry to work at the intersection of science, evidence, and policymaking.

Now in its fourth year, the Defra R&D Fellowship Programme has become one of the UK’s leading policy-focused fellowship opportunities, giving researchers the chance to spend up to 12 months working directly within government while helping shape policies on environmental protection, climate change, agriculture, biodiversity, food security, and many other national priorities.

If you are passionate about using scientific research and analytical expertise to solve complex societal challenges, this fellowship offers an outstanding platform to expand your career while influencing evidence-based government decisions.

About the Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) is responsible for some of the UK’s most important public policy areas, including environmental protection, sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, food production, water systems, biodiversity, and national environmental security.

Through the Research and Development Fellowship Programme, Defra brings together talented researchers and analysts from universities, research institutions, and industry to contribute their expertise to government projects.

Rather than remaining solely within academic or industrial research environments, fellows gain first-hand experience of how scientific evidence is translated into practical government policy. The programme is specifically designed to strengthen collaboration between the research community and policymakers.

Why This Fellowship Is Unique

Unlike many traditional research fellowships, the Defra R&D Fellowship focuses on policy impact. Fellows become embedded within Defra’s science, evidence, and policy teams, where they contribute directly to projects that influence national decision-making.

As a fellow, you will:

  • Work alongside government scientists, analysts, and policy experts.

  • Apply your research expertise to real public policy challenges.

  • Contribute to national environmental and agricultural strategies.

  • Build strong professional networks across government and research institutions.

  • Develop valuable policy, communication, and leadership skills.

  • Experience how evidence informs government decisions.

Fellowship Duration

Successful applicants will join Defra on a short-term appointment lasting between six months and one year.

Key dates include:

Defra also offers flexibility in certain circumstances, including secondment arrangements for applicants who wish to remain employed by their current institution while participating in the fellowship.

Areas You Could Work On

The fellowship covers a wide range of research and policy areas across Defra’s responsibilities. Fellows may contribute to projects involving:

Environmental Protection

  • Biodiversity conservation

  • Ecosystem restoration

  • Nature recovery

  • Wildlife protection

  • Air quality improvement

  • Marine and freshwater ecosystems

Climate Change and Sustainability

  • Climate adaptation

  • Climate resilience

  • Carbon reduction strategies

  • Environmental risk assessment

  • Sustainable resource management

Food and Agriculture

  • Sustainable food production

  • Farming innovation

  • Agricultural policy

  • Animal health and welfare

  • Plant science

  • Fisheries management

Science, Data, and Innovation

  • Artificial intelligence applications

  • Data science

  • Statistical analysis

  • Environmental modelling

  • Geographic analysis

  • Operational research

  • Scientific evidence synthesis

National Security and Environmental Risk

  • Natural hazards

  • Biosecurity

  • Environmental resilience

  • Risk management

  • Public safety initiatives

Because Defra’s work spans numerous disciplines, fellows from diverse scientific and analytical backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

What You Will Be Doing as a Defra Fellow

During your fellowship, you will become an integral member of a Defra team. Your responsibilities may include:

  • Conducting high-quality scientific or analytical research.

  • Supporting the development of government policies.

  • Synthesizing complex research evidence.

  • Communicating scientific findings to policymakers.

  • Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams.

  • Working with Defra’s public sector research establishments.

  • Engaging with stakeholders from academia, government, and industry.

  • Supporting innovation across environmental and agricultural programmes.

Rather than working in isolation, fellows collaborate with professionals from different disciplines, creating an exciting environment where research directly influences public policy.

Benefits of the Defra R&D Fellowship Programme

The programme offers numerous professional and career development benefits.

1. Work on High-Impact National Projects

Your research can directly influence UK government decisions on issues such as climate change, environmental protection, food systems, biodiversity, and public resilience.

2. Gain Policy Experience

Many researchers have limited exposure to policymaking. This fellowship provides valuable insight into how government develops evidence-based policies.

3. Build a Strong Professional Network

Fellows work closely with:

  • Government scientists

  • Policy advisers

  • Analysts

  • Academic researchers

  • Public sector organisations

  • Industry experts

4. Develop Transferable Skills

Participants strengthen skills in:

  • Policy writing

  • Scientific communication

  • Stakeholder engagement

  • Evidence synthesis

  • Project management

  • Leadership

  • Cross-disciplinary collaboration

5. Career Development

Previous fellows have highlighted the programme as an excellent stepping stone into careers in:

  • Government research

  • Public policy

  • Civil Service

  • Academic leadership

  • Research management

  • Environmental consultancy

6. Competitive Salary

Successful fellows receive a salary funded by Defra.

Who Should Apply?

Defra welcomes applications from researchers at different career stages.

The fellowship is particularly suitable for:

  • Early-career researchers.

  • Mid-career researchers.

  • Experienced scientists.

  • Analysts seeking policy experience.

  • Researchers from academia.

  • Professionals working in industry.

  • Technical specialists interested in public policy.

Importantly, previous policy experience is not required. Defra provides opportunities for fellows to develop policy knowledge throughout the programme.

Eligible Academic and Professional Backgrounds

Applicants from a broad range of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including:

Scientific Disciplines

  • Environmental science

  • Biological sciences

  • Agricultural sciences

  • Plant sciences

  • Animal sciences

Engineering Fields

  • Agricultural engineering

  • Civil engineering

  • Systems engineering

Analytical Professions

  • Statistics

  • Economics

  • Social research

  • Operational research

  • Data science

  • Geography

  • Artificial intelligence

  • Machine learning

Defra is actively seeking people with strong scientific or analytical expertise who can contribute fresh perspectives to government projects.

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible, applicants should meet one of the following academic or professional pathways.

Option 1

You have:

  • An undergraduate degree in a science, engineering, or analytical discipline.

  • A postgraduate degree (or expect to complete one before 1 April 2027).

Option 2

You are:

  • A Chartered Engineer.

  • A Chartered Scientist registered through an appropriate professional institution recognised by the Engineering Council or Science Council.

Applicants must also demonstrate:

  • Strong technical expertise.

  • Excellent communication skills.

  • Motivation to contribute to public policy.

  • Interest in evidence-based decision-making.

  • Ability to work collaboratively across disciplines.

    What Skills Does Defra Look For?

Successful applicants typically demonstrate:

  • Scientific excellence.

  • Analytical thinking.

  • Research expertise.

  • Critical problem-solving.

  • Strong written communication.

  • Ability to explain complex ideas clearly.

  • Stakeholder engagement skills.

  • Teamwork and collaboration.

  • Adaptability in fast-paced environments.

  • Interest in innovation and public service.

How the Application Process Works

The application process is completed online through the UK Civil Service Careers portal.

Applicants will be required to submit:

  1. Employment history.

  2. Educational qualifications.

  3. Online application form.

  4. A 500-word personal statement explaining:

    • Relevant experience.

    • Technical expertise.

    • Motivation for joining Defra.

    • Interest in the chosen policy area.

  5. Preferred policy areas.

After applications close:

  • Applications will be shortlisted.

  • Selected candidates will attend virtual interviews.

  • Successful applicants will be matched with suitable Defra projects.

  • A reserve list may also be created for future opportunities.

Selection Process

Defra assesses candidates based on several important criteria.

These include:

  • Scientific or analytical expertise.

  • Technical knowledge.

  • Communication skills.

  • Motivation for the fellowship.

  • Relevant research experience.

  • Ability to contribute to policy-focused projects.

Virtual interviews will be conducted with relevant Defra science and analysis teams.

What Previous Fellows Have Gained

Past participants have described the fellowship as a transformative professional experience.

According to former fellows, the programme has helped them:

  • Transition from academia into policy.

  • Learn government decision-making processes.

  • Develop AI and data science skills.

  • Lead important environmental research projects.

  • Expand professional networks.

  • Build expertise in project management.

  • Gain experience communicating science to policymakers.

Several fellows have worked on projects involving environmental monitoring, fisheries management, modelling, biodiversity, and innovative research methods.

The Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme offers much more than a traditional research placement. It is an opportunity to:

  • Expand your professional network.

Whether your long-term career is in academia, government, research, or industry, this fellowship provides unique experience that can significantly strengthen your professional profile.

The Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme 2027/28 is an outstanding opportunity for scientists, engineers, and analytical professionals who want to see their research make a tangible difference in society. With competitive salaries, flexible working arrangements, extensive networking opportunities, and the chance to influence evidence-based government policy, this fellowship is an excellent career development opportunity for researchers at both early and mid-career stages. item.content:encoded:
The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026 offers an exciting research opportunity for doctoral candidates enrolled at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities to undertake dissertation-related research at the Smithsonian Institution. The fellowship is designed for advanced doctoral students who have completed their coursework, have been admitted to doctoral candidacy, and have fulfilled all degree requirements except the completion of their dissertation. Selected fellows can conduct research and scholarship at the Smithsonian under the guidance of an appropriate Smithsonian adviser, with the goal of strengthening and advancing their doctoral thesis. The fellowship provides a stipend of $45,000 per year, along with a research allowance of up to $5,000 per year. Fellowship appointments can last from 3 to 12 months, with stipends prorated for periods shorter than one year. Applications for the 2026 competition must be submitted by October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) through the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program application system.

Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026 Overview

The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship brings together doctoral research communities from participating Big Ten universities and the Smithsonian Institution.

The program is intended to help advanced doctoral candidates access Smithsonian research resources, collections, expertise and scholarly networks that can contribute substantially to their dissertation research.

Key details at a glance

  • Program: Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship
  • Host institution: Smithsonian Institution
  • Participating universities: Big Ten Academic Alliance member institutions
  • Duration: 3 to 12 months
  • Stipend: $45,000 per year
  • Research allowance: Up to $5,000 per year
  • Application deadline: October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET
  • Eligible applicants: Currently enrolled doctoral candidates at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities
  • Citizenship: Open to both U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens
  • Application language: English
  • Application platform: Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP)

What Is the Big Ten Academic Alliance?

The Big Ten Academic Alliance is a consortium of research universities that was established in 1958.

The alliance enables its member institutions to collaborate on academic and administrative initiatives designed to strengthen their educational and research missions. Through collaboration, the universities share expertise, leverage resources and create opportunities for students and faculty.

The alliance also seeks to support initiatives that contribute to the broader common good by encouraging collaboration and innovation across its member institutions.

The Smithsonian Fellowship is one example of this collaborative approach, providing eligible doctoral candidates with an opportunity to conduct research within the Smithsonian environment while advancing their dissertation work.

Universities Participating in the Program

The current Big Ten Academic Alliance institutions participating in the fellowship include:

  • University of Illinois
  • Indiana University
  • University of Iowa
  • University of Maryland
  • University of Michigan
  • University of Oregon
  • University of Washington
  • Michigan State University
  • University of Minnesota
  • University of Nebraska-Lincoln
  • Northwestern University
  • Ohio State University
  • University of California, Los Angeles
  • Pennsylvania State University
  • Purdue University
  • Rutgers University-New Brunswick
  • University of Wisconsin-Madison
  • University of Southern California
  • University of Chicago

The University of Chicago participates in the program as an affiliate.

Students should verify their university’s current participation and consult their campus Big Ten Academic Alliance fellowship contact before preparing an application.

Purpose of the Smithsonian Fellowship

The primary purpose of the program is to support advanced doctoral research.

The fellowship targets students who have reached a particularly important stage of their doctoral programs: they have completed their coursework and advanced to doctoral candidacy, but have not yet completed their dissertation.

At this stage, access to specialised research collections, laboratories, archives, experts and other academic resources can be extremely valuable.

The program allows eligible doctoral candidates to identify an appropriate adviser at the Smithsonian and conduct research or scholarship that contributes to the development and completion of their dissertation.

Rather than being a general graduate scholarship, the fellowship is therefore closely connected to a candidate’s existing doctoral research.

Research Areas Covered by the Fellowship

Applicants must propose research that will be conducted at the Smithsonian in an eligible research area.

The program covers a broad range of disciplines, allowing doctoral candidates from different academic backgrounds to develop research projects that align with Smithsonian expertise and resources.

Eligible areas include:

1. Animal Behavior, Ecology and Environmental Science

Research can focus on animal behavior, ecology and environmental science, including research with an emphasis on tropical environments.

This area may be particularly relevant to doctoral candidates researching biodiversity, ecosystems, species behavior, environmental change and related scientific questions.

2. Anthropology

The fellowship supports research in anthropology, including:

  • Archaeology
  • Cultural anthropology
  • Linguistics
  • Physical anthropology

Doctoral candidates conducting research involving human societies, cultures, languages, archaeological evidence or human biological variation may find this research area particularly relevant.

3. Earth Sciences and Paleobiology

Applicants can also propose research involving Earth sciences and paleobiology.

This area provides opportunities for researchers whose doctoral work focuses on Earth’s history, geological processes, fossils, ancient life and related scientific questions.

4. Evolutionary and Systematic Biology

The program supports research in evolutionary and systematic biology.

This may include doctoral research focused on evolutionary relationships, biological diversity, classification and the study of organisms and their development over time.

5. Folklife

Folklife is another eligible area of research.

Doctoral candidates whose work examines cultural traditions, everyday practices, community knowledge and related forms of cultural expression may be able to develop research projects within this area.

6. History of Science and Technology

Research concerning the history of science and technology is also eligible.

This may be relevant to doctoral candidates studying the development of scientific knowledge, technological change, scientific institutions, inventions and the relationship between science, technology and society.

7. History of Art

The fellowship supports history of art research, with particular emphasis on areas including:

  • American art
  • Contemporary art
  • African art
  • Asian art
  • Twentieth-century American crafts
  • Decorative arts

Doctoral candidates whose dissertations involve art history or related scholarly research may benefit from access to Smithsonian collections, expertise and resources.

8. Materials Research

Materials research is included among the eligible research areas.

This provides opportunities for doctoral candidates whose research involves the study, properties, development or application of materials.

9. Molecular Biology

The fellowship also supports molecular biology research.

This can be relevant to doctoral research involving biological molecules, cellular processes, genetics and related areas of molecular science.

10. Social and Cultural History of the United States

Applicants can also propose research focused on the social and cultural history of the United States.

This may include research examining American communities, social developments, cultural change, historical experiences and other aspects of the country’s social and cultural development.

Who Is Eligible for the Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship?

Eligibility is relatively specific because this fellowship is intended for doctoral candidates enrolled at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities.

Applicants must be currently enrolled at one of the eligible Big Ten Academic Alliance member universities.

In addition, candidates must satisfy specific doctoral-stage requirements.

Doctoral requirements

By the time the fellowship appointment begins, applicants must have:

  1. Completed all coursework required for their doctoral program.
  2. Been admitted to doctoral candidacy.
  3. Satisfied all doctoral requirements except completion of the dissertation.

This means the fellowship is designed for advanced doctoral candidates who are already at the dissertation stage rather than students who are just beginning their doctoral programs.

Citizenship and Nationality Eligibility

The fellowship is open to both U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens.

Therefore, citizenship does not appear to be restricted to applicants from the United States.

However, applicants must still meet the central institutional eligibility requirement: they must be currently enrolled at one of the participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities and satisfy the doctoral candidacy and coursework requirements.

For international doctoral candidates, this is an important distinction. Being a non-U.S. citizen does not automatically prevent participation, provided the applicant meets the program’s other eligibility conditions.

English Language Requirement

Applicants whose native language is not English are expected to have the ability to write and converse fluently in English.

All application materials must be presented in English.

International applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate that they can effectively communicate their research, academic qualifications and proposed work in written and spoken English.

Finding a Smithsonian Adviser

An important element of the fellowship is identifying an appropriate adviser at the Smithsonian.

The doctoral candidate’s research proposal should be compatible with the research expertise and resources available at the Smithsonian.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider which Smithsonian researcher, curator, scientist, scholar or relevant specialist may be an appropriate adviser for their proposed research.

A strong alignment between the candidate’s dissertation project and available Smithsonian expertise can be an important part of developing a compelling research proposal.

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship appointment can last from 3 to 12 months.

This flexibility allows doctoral candidates to structure the fellowship period around their research requirements.

A candidate may need a shorter appointment for a specific research project, collection-based investigation or period of specialised work, while another candidate may benefit from a longer appointment to conduct extensive dissertation research.

For appointments lasting less than 12 months, the fellowship stipend is prorated.

Fellowship Stipend and Research Allowance

The financial support provided through the program consists of two major components.

$45,000 annual stipend

Fellows receive a stipend of $45,000 per year.

For fellowship appointments shorter than 12 months, the stipend is prorated according to the length of the appointment.

For example, a fellow appointed for only part of the year would not receive the full annual amount; the amount would be adjusted based on the fellowship period.

Up to $5,000 research allowance

In addition to the stipend, fellows can receive a research allowance of up to $5,000 per year.

This additional funding can provide support for eligible research-related expenses associated with carrying out the proposed scholarly work.

Applicants should consult the official program guidelines for the precise rules governing allowable research expenses.

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Doctoral Researchers

The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship can be particularly valuable for doctoral candidates whose dissertation research would benefit from Smithsonian expertise, collections or research facilities.

Some of the potential advantages include:

Access to a major research environment

The Smithsonian is a globally recognised research and cultural institution with extensive collections, expertise and scholarly resources.

Conducting dissertation research within this environment can provide doctoral candidates with access to resources that may not be readily available at their home institution.

Dedicated time for dissertation research

The fellowship provides an opportunity for advanced doctoral candidates to devote a defined period to their research.

Having a fellowship appointment can help candidates focus on completing important stages of their dissertation work.

Research collaboration and mentorship

Working with an appropriate Smithsonian adviser can provide specialised academic guidance and create opportunities for collaboration.

This can be especially useful when a dissertation requires expertise that complements the candidate’s university-based supervision.

Financial support

The $45,000 annual stipend provides substantial financial support during the fellowship period.

The additional research allowance of up to $5,000 per year can further support eligible research activities.

Interdisciplinary research opportunities

The wide range of eligible research fields makes the program relevant to doctoral candidates working across science, humanities, social sciences, anthropology, environmental research, art history and other disciplines.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Although meeting the eligibility requirements is essential, candidates should also focus on developing a clear and well-supported application.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the connection between the applicant’s doctoral research and the Smithsonian environment.

Step 1: Confirm your university eligibility

First, verify that your university is a current participating Big Ten Academic Alliance institution or affiliate participating in the program.

Step 2: Confirm your doctoral status

Ensure that you will have completed all coursework, been admitted to doctoral candidacy and satisfied all requirements except the dissertation by the time the fellowship begins.

Step 3: Define your research objectives

Clearly explain what you intend to accomplish during the fellowship.

Your proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand:

  • The research question
  • The significance of the research
  • How the research relates to your dissertation
  • Why the Smithsonian is an appropriate place to conduct the work
  • What resources or expertise you need
  • What you expect to accomplish during the fellowship

Step 4: Identify a suitable Smithsonian adviser

Research the Smithsonian’s relevant scholars, scientists, curators and research resources to identify potential advisers whose expertise aligns with your dissertation.

Step 5: Connect the research to Smithsonian resources

Explain why conducting the research at the Smithsonian is important.

A convincing proposal should demonstrate that the Smithsonian environment offers meaningful resources, collections, expertise or facilities that will strengthen the dissertation.

Step 6: Review the application requirements

Applicants should carefully read the official Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program guidelines and make sure all required materials are prepared in English.

Step 7: Submit before the deadline

Do not wait until the final hours to submit.

The deadline is October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Applicants should allow sufficient time to review their application and resolve any submission issues before the deadline.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship is:

October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET).

All applications must be submitted through the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP) application system by the stated deadline.

Applicants should pay attention to the time zone because the deadline is specified in Eastern Time.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP).

Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP) – Official Application and Program Guidelines

Applicants should review the program guidelines carefully before beginning the application process.

The official program information should be treated as the authoritative source for application requirements, supporting documents, procedures and any updates to the competition.

Big Ten Campus Fellowship Contacts

The program provides information about Smithsonian Fellowship contacts at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance campuses.

These campus contacts can be particularly useful for prospective applicants because they may provide university-specific guidance concerning the fellowship and application process.

Applicants should consult the Big Ten Academic Alliance’s Smithsonian Fellowship information for the relevant contact at their institution.

Important Things to Remember Before Applying

Prospective applicants should keep the following points in mind:

  • The fellowship is specifically intended for doctoral candidates at participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities.
  • Applicants must be currently enrolled at an eligible university.
  • Applicants must have completed their doctoral coursework.
  • Applicants must have been admitted to doctoral candidacy by the time the fellowship begins.
  • Applicants must have fulfilled all requirements except completion of the dissertation.
  • The program is open to both U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens.
  • Applicants whose native language is not English must be able to write and converse fluently in English.
  • All application materials must be submitted in English.
  • Proposed research must fall within one of the program’s specified research areas.
  • Applicants should identify an appropriate Smithsonian adviser for their research.
  • Fellowship appointments last between 3 and 12 months.
  • The annual stipend is $45,000.
  • A research allowance of up to $5,000 per year is available.
  • Stipends are prorated for appointments shorter than 12 months.
  • Applications must be submitted by October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
  • Applicants should carefully review the official SIFP guidelines before submitting an application.

Learn more HERE

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship?

It is a fellowship program designed to support advanced doctoral candidates from participating Big Ten Academic Alliance universities in conducting dissertation-related research at the Smithsonian Institution.

How much is the fellowship stipend?

The fellowship provides a stipend of $45,000 per year, prorated for appointments of less than 12 months.

Is there additional research funding?

Yes. Fellows can receive a research allowance of up to $5,000 per year.

How long is the fellowship?

Appointments can last between 3 and 12 months.

Can international students apply?

Yes. The program is open to U.S. citizens and non-U.S. citizens. However, applicants must meet the university enrollment and doctoral-stage requirements.

Do applicants have to be doctoral candidates?

Yes. Applicants must be admitted to doctoral candidacy and have completed all requirements except the dissertation by the time their fellowship appointment begins.

Can students who have not completed their coursework apply?

The eligibility requirements state that students must have completed all coursework for their programs by the time the appointment begins.

What research fields are eligible?

Eligible areas include animal behavior, ecology and environmental science; anthropology; Earth sciences and paleobiology; evolutionary and systematic biology; folklife; history of science and technology; history of art; materials research; molecular biology; and social and cultural history of the United States.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is October 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Where do applicants apply?

Applications are submitted through the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program.

Conclusion

The Big Ten Academic Alliance Smithsonian Fellowship 2026 is a significant research opportunity for advanced doctoral candidates seeking to strengthen their dissertation work through research at the Smithsonian Institution.

With a $45,000 annual stipend, an additional research allowance of up to $5,000 per year, and flexible fellowship appointments of 3 to 12 months, the program offers both financial and academic support to eligible researchers.

The fellowship is particularly attractive to doctoral candidates whose work aligns with the Smithsonian’s broad research strengths, including environmental science, anthropology, Earth sciences, biology, folklife, history, art history, materials research, molecular biology and U.S. social and cultural history.

Because eligibility is tied to enrollment at a participating Big Ten Academic Alliance university and advanced doctoral status, prospective applicants should confirm their eligibility well before beginning the application. They should also identify a suitable Smithsonian adviser and demonstrate clearly why conducting their research at the Smithsonian would advance their dissertation.

Most importantly, eligible candidates should prepare their applications well in advance of the October 15, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET deadline. Reviewing the official Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program guidelines and consulting the appropriate fellowship contact at their university can help applicants understand the requirements and submit a complete application on time.
