item.content:encoded:
Chatham House is inviting applications for a Research Associate – Digital Society Programme, an exciting opportunity for professionals interested in emerging technologies, digital policy, geopolitics, political economy and technology governance.

The position is based in London, United Kingdom, within Chatham House’s Research Department and offers the successful candidate the opportunity to contribute to high-impact research examining how emerging technologies are shaping states, companies, societies and international affairs.

The role is particularly suited to candidates who combine strong research and analytical abilities with technical knowledge of emerging technologies and an interest in their wider political, economic and societal implications.

About the Chatham House Digital Society Programme

The Digital Society Programme at Chatham House examines the rapidly changing relationship between technology, politics and international affairs.

The programme focuses on the geopolitics and political economy of emerging technology, exploring how governments, businesses and other stakeholders can develop the digital infrastructure and governance systems necessary to maintain agency in an increasingly technology-driven world.

Its work goes beyond simply analysing technological developments. The programme also explores practical approaches to governing, scaling and managing emerging digital infrastructure.

An important aspect of the programme is its ability to connect different communities. It works across multilateral forums, technology communities, governments, companies, researchers and other stakeholders, helping to bridge the gap between technological developments and policy-making.

For a Research Associate, this creates an opportunity to work at the intersection of:

  • Emerging technologies
  • International relations
  • Geopolitics
  • Political economy
  • Digital governance
  • Technology policy
  • Research and analysis
  • Public policy
  • Multilateral engagement
  • Stakeholder engagement

What Will the Research Associate Do?

The successful candidate will support the delivery of research projects and contribute to the development of policy-relevant work within the Digital Society Programme.

The position combines research, technology, communication, event coordination and stakeholder engagement responsibilities, making it suitable for professionals who can operate across several areas.

1. Support High-Impact Research Projects

A major responsibility of the Research Associate will be supporting the delivery of research projects undertaken by the Digital Society Programme.

This will require the candidate to contribute to research activities that address contemporary questions surrounding emerging technologies and their implications for governments, societies, businesses and the international system.

The successful candidate may therefore be expected to:

  • Conduct research and analysis.
  • Support research project delivery.
  • Contribute to evidence-based policy work.
  • Investigate emerging technology trends.
  • Examine the societal and political implications of technological developments.
  • Help translate complex research into useful policy insights.
  • Contribute to research outputs and project deliverables.

The role is therefore particularly relevant for applicants who enjoy combining technology, research and public policy.

2. Conduct Policy-Relevant Research

The position will involve conducting research that is not purely academic but is designed to contribute to real-world policy discussions.

The Research Associate will be expected to understand emerging technologies and assess their broader implications for society, governments and other stakeholders.

This could involve examining questions such as the following:

  • How are emerging technologies changing international relations?
  • What technological capabilities do states require to maintain strategic autonomy?
  • What are the political and economic consequences of emerging digital infrastructure?
  • How should governments and other stakeholders approach technology governance?
  • What societal implications arise from rapid technological change?
  • How can emerging technologies be responsibly scaled and managed?

The ability to move from technical information to clear, practical policy conclusions will therefore be important.

3. Use Emerging Technologies to Innovate Research Delivery

The position places particular emphasis on technical skills and emerging technologies.

The successful candidate will be expected to demonstrate outstanding fluency in using emerging technologies as they relate to policy research.

This means applicants should be comfortable exploring how new technologies can improve the way research is conducted, analysed, communicated and delivered.

The role provides an opportunity for someone who understands not only emerging technologies themselves but also how those technologies can be applied to research and policy work.

4. Present Technical Findings Clearly

Research findings are only useful when they can be communicated effectively to the intended audience.

The Research Associate will therefore be expected to present technical research findings in ways that are clear, accessible and creative.

This responsibility requires the ability to communicate complex technological and policy issues to different audiences, potentially including:

  • Policymakers
  • Researchers
  • Government officials
  • Technology professionals
  • International stakeholders
  • Civil society
  • Businesses
  • Multilateral organisations
  • General audiences interested in technology and global affairs

Candidates should therefore possess strong written, analytical and verbal communication abilities.

5. Plan and Coordinate Events

The Research Associate will also contribute to the organisation and delivery of events associated with the Digital Society Programme.

These may include:

  • Expert panels
  • Policy discussions
  • Scenario exercises
  • Stakeholder meetings
  • Research-related events
  • Other programme activities

This means the role is not limited to desk-based research. The successful candidate will also have opportunities to participate in activities that bring researchers, policymakers, technology experts and other stakeholders together.

Strong organisational and coordination skills will consequently be important.

6. Contribute to Fundraising and New Projects

Another important component of the position is supporting fundraising and the development of new project opportunities.

The Research Associate may contribute to activities associated with identifying, developing and supporting potential research projects.

Experience with research proposals, project development or stakeholder engagement can therefore be valuable for applicants seeking to demonstrate their suitability for the role.

Skills and Experience Chatham House Is Looking For

Chatham House is looking for a candidate who can combine technical expertise, research capability, policy understanding and excellent organisational skills.

Technical Knowledge of Emerging Technologies

Applicants should have strong technical skills and outstanding fluency in the application of emerging technologies to policy research.

This is one of the defining requirements of the role.

Candidates should be able to demonstrate that they understand emerging technologies and can consider their practical applications within research and policy environments.

Understanding of the Technical and Societal Implications of Technology

The successful applicant should possess expertise in both the technical and societal dimensions of emerging technologies.

This is important because the Digital Society Programme considers technology not only as a technical subject but also as an issue affecting politics, economics, societies and international relations.

A strong candidate should therefore be able to consider both:

  1. What a technology does technically, and
  2. What that technology means for society, governments, businesses and international affairs.

Ability to Manage Multiple Priorities

The Research Associate will likely work across different projects and programme activities.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate the ability to:

  • Organise competing tasks.
  • Meet deadlines.
  • Prioritise effectively.
  • Work on several projects simultaneously.
  • Adapt to changing requirements.
  • Maintain quality while handling multiple responsibilities.

Collaboration and Teamwork

The position requires someone who can work collaboratively with colleagues and external stakeholders.

Applicants should be comfortable contributing to team-based research and working with people from different professional and technical backgrounds.

Organisation and Attention to Detail

Strong organisational skills will be essential, particularly given the combination of research, events, stakeholder engagement and project responsibilities.

Attention to detail will also be important when conducting research, preparing outputs, coordinating events and supporting project development.

Problem-Solving Skills

The successful candidate should have strong problem-solving abilities and be capable of approaching complex research and technology-related questions systematically.

This is particularly important in a field where technological developments can change rapidly and where policy challenges may not have straightforward solutions.

Research Proposals, Events and Stakeholder Engagement

Experience supporting research proposals, events or stakeholder engagement will be relevant to the role.

Applicants should highlight practical examples demonstrating their ability to contribute to research projects, coordinate activities or engage effectively with relevant stakeholders.

Employment Details

The Research Associate position offers a full-time, permanent contract.

Key employment details include:

  • Job title: Research Associate – Digital Society Programme
  • Department: Research
  • Organisation: Chatham House
  • Location: St James’s Square, London
  • Contract: Full-time and permanent
  • Salary: £38,000 per year
  • Working arrangement: Hybrid
  • Office requirement: At least two days per week onsite
  • Additional flexibility: Flexibility may be required around events
  • Application deadline: Monday, 7 September 2026 at 23:59 BST

Applicants should ensure that they submit their applications before the stated deadline.

Employee Benefits

Chatham House offers a range of benefits alongside the advertised salary.

These include approximately 37 days of annual leave, incorporating public holidays and Chatham House closure days.

Other benefits include:

  • Pension salary exchange
  • Employee assistance programme
  • Parental leave
  • Flexible working
  • Additional lifestyle-oriented employee benefits

The organisation describes the working environment as professional, engaging and intellectually stimulating.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for Your Career

The Research Associate position could be particularly valuable for professionals seeking to build a career at the intersection of technology, international affairs, public policy and research.

The role provides exposure to research questions concerning some of the most important technological developments shaping the contemporary world.

A successful candidate could gain experience in areas such as:

Emerging Technology Policy

The role provides an opportunity to examine how emerging technologies interact with government policy, international affairs and society.

Technology and Geopolitics

Because the Digital Society Programme focuses on the geopolitics of emerging technology, the position offers an opportunity to contribute to discussions about technology and global power.

Political Economy of Technology

The programme also investigates the political economy of emerging technologies, providing exposure to questions involving states, markets, companies and digital infrastructure.

Policy Research

The position provides hands-on experience in producing research intended to inform policy discussions rather than simply academic debate.

International Stakeholder Engagement

The programme’s work across multilateral forums and technology communities means that the successful candidate can potentially gain valuable experience engaging with diverse stakeholders.

Research Communication

The ability to translate technical research into clear and creative outputs is increasingly valuable across government, international organisations, think tanks, academia and the private sector.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Candidates should ensure that their application directly demonstrates how their background matches the requirements of the Research Associate position.

Rather than simply listing qualifications, applicants can strengthen their application by providing evidence of relevant experience.

For example, candidates may wish to demonstrate the following:

  1. Experience with emerging technologies – Explain which technologies you have worked with or researched and how you applied them.
  2. Technology-policy expertise – Show how you have examined the implications of technology for governments, society, businesses or international affairs.
  3. Research experience – Provide examples of research projects, policy analysis, reports, publications or other relevant outputs.
  4. Communication skills – Demonstrate your ability to explain complex technical issues to non-technical audiences.
  5. Event coordination – Highlight experience organising conferences, panels, workshops, scenario exercises or stakeholder meetings.
  6. Stakeholder engagement – Provide examples of working with policymakers, researchers, technology professionals, institutions or other stakeholders.
  7. Project management – Show how you have managed competing deadlines, responsibilities and priorities.
  8. Research proposals and fundraising—If applicable, highlight experience supporting proposals, developing project concepts or contributing to fundraising activities.
  9. Problem-solving – Use practical examples to demonstrate how you addressed complex challenges.
  10. Innovation – Explain how you have used emerging technologies or innovative approaches to improve research, analysis or communication.

Who Can Apply?

The vacancy states that Chatham House is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from people from all backgrounds.

The organisation states that it values diversity and does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics.

The vacancy does not specify a particular race, ethnicity or continent as an eligibility restriction, meaning the advertisement is open to candidates from all backgrounds rather than being restricted to a particular racial group or continent.

However, applicants should note that this is a London-based hybrid position, with the successful candidate expected to work onsite at the London office at least two days each week, with additional flexibility required around events.

The advertisement provided does not specify a particular nationality requirement or explicitly state that applicants from a particular country are eligible or ineligible. Applicants should therefore check the full vacancy information and ensure that they meet any applicable UK employment or work-authorisation requirements before applying.

Qualifications and Professional Profile

The ideal applicant is someone with a combination of:

  • Strong technical skills.
  • Excellent knowledge of emerging technologies.
  • Understanding of the societal implications of emerging technology.
  • Understanding of technology-related policy issues.
  • Strong research and analytical capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organisational abilities.
  • Attention to detail.
  • Problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to work collaboratively.
  • Experience supporting research projects, proposals, events or stakeholder engagement.

Candidates whose professional backgrounds combine technology, research, international affairs, public policy, digital governance, political economy or related areas may find the opportunity particularly relevant, provided they can demonstrate the technical and research capabilities required by the vacancy.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Chatham House Research Associate – Digital Society Programme position is:

Monday, 7 September 2026, at 23:59 BST.

Applicants are encouraged to complete their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical or submission problems.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should review the complete vacancy information and submit their application through the official Chatham House careers platform.

Applicants should also review the full job description before applying to ensure that they understand the complete requirements, responsibilities and application process.

Visit HERE for more information about the Chatham House Research Associate – Digital Society Programme.

Conclusion

The Chatham House Research Associate – Digital Society Programme position is a strong opportunity for professionals interested in the rapidly evolving relationship between emerging technology, geopolitics, public policy and society.

With a £38,000 annual salary, a full-time permanent contract, hybrid working in London and a comprehensive benefits package, the position offers an opportunity to contribute to high-impact research while working within an internationally recognised research environment.

The successful candidate will be expected to go beyond conventional research by combining technical understanding with policy analysis, stakeholder engagement, event coordination and effective communication. The role is particularly relevant to professionals who can understand emerging technologies while also analysing their wider political, economic and societal consequences.

Candidates should pay close attention to the technical and research requirements and use their applications to demonstrate concrete examples of their experience, rather than relying solely on general statements about their skills.

item.content:encoded:
The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) is accepting applications for its Economic and Environmental Dimension Internship 2026, offering students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain practical international experience at the OSCE Secretariat in Vienna, Austria, with an additional duty location in Prague, Czechia.

The internship is designed for emerging professionals interested in areas including economics, environmental affairs, sustainable development, international development, finance, good governance, anti-corruption, natural-resource management, environmental security and related policy fields.

Successful candidates may undertake an internship lasting between two and six months, working alongside OSCE professionals in a multinational institutional environment. The internship can involve policy research, project management, drafting reports and briefing materials, financial analysis, event organization, communications, administrative support and engagement with internal and external stakeholders.

The vacancy was issued by the OSCE Secretariat under Requisition SEC001012. Multiple internship positions are available, and the official closing date is December 31, 2026.

OSCE Economic and Environmental Dimension Internship 2026 at a Glance

Organization: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe
Programme: Internship – Economic and Environmental Dimension
Requisition ID: SEC001012
Primary Location: OSCE Secretariat, Vienna, Austria
Additional Location: OSCE Secretariat, Prague, Czechia
Number of Positions: Multiple
Duration: 2–6 months
Schedule: Primarily full-time
Working Hours: Approximately 40 hours per week
Job Field: Administration & Support
Contract Type: Intern
Issue Date: July 3, 2026
Application Deadline: December 31, 2026
Age Limit: Applicants must not be older than 30 on the vacancy deadline.

About the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe

The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe is a major intergovernmental security organization bringing together 57 participating States across North America, Europe and Asia.

Its work is based on the principle that security cannot be viewed purely through military or political considerations. Instead, lasting peace and stability also depend on economic development, environmental protection, democratic institutions, human rights, good governance and cooperation between states.

The OSCE organizes much of its work around three broad dimensions:

  1. The politico-military dimension;
  2. The economic and environmental dimension; and
  3. The human dimension.

The organization works to promote stability, peace and security for more than one billion people through political dialogue and practical programmes implemented across its region.

Understanding the OSCE Economic and Environmental Dimension

The internship specifically focuses on the OSCE’s Economic and Environmental Dimension, sometimes referred to as the organization’s second dimension.

The foundations of this dimension can be traced to the Helsinki Final Act, where participating States recognized the importance of cooperation in economics, science, technology and environmental affairs.

The principle behind this work is that economic and environmental problems can have consequences extending well beyond development policy. When issues such as corruption, economic inequality, poor natural-resource governance, environmental degradation or ineffective waste management are not adequately addressed, they can contribute to instability and tensions within or between countries.

Development of the OSCE’s Economic and Environmental Work

The OSCE’s economic and environmental mandate has evolved over several decades.

An important milestone was the Conference on Economic Co-operation in Europe held in Bonn in 1990, where participating States emphasized common objectives such as sustainable economic growth, improving living standards and quality of life, creating employment, using economic resources efficiently and protecting the environment.

The OSCE subsequently developed institutional mechanisms addressing economic and environmental security, including the work of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities and the Economic and Environmental Forum.

Another major milestone came during the 2003 Maastricht Ministerial Council meeting, when participating States adopted the OSCE Strategy Document for the Economic and Environmental Dimension.

This strengthened cooperation in fields including:

  • Economic development;
  • Good governance;
  • Sustainable development;
  • Environmental protection; and
  • Economic and environmental security.

The internship therefore sits within a substantial policy framework connecting economics and environmental issues with wider international security and stability.

What Does the Economic and Environmental Dimension Work On?

Through this dimension, the OSCE assists participating States with challenges that can potentially affect security and stability.

Relevant areas include:

  • Good governance;
  • Environmental awareness;
  • Anti-corruption initiatives;
  • Sustainable development;
  • Natural-resource management;
  • Sharing of natural resources;
  • Environmental waste management;
  • Economic governance;
  • Environmental protection;
  • Economic and environmental security; and
  • Related policy and programme development.

Interns may therefore gain exposure to topics that connect international relations with economics, sustainability and environmental governance.

What Can the OSCE Internship Programme Offer?

The internship provides young professionals with an opportunity to experience the daily working environment of a major multilateral organization.

1. Practical Exposure to an International Organization

Interns can gain direct insight into how the OSCE Secretariat operates and how international institutions translate policy commitments into programmes, research, meetings, projects and administrative activities.

2. Professional Skills Development

The internship gives participants opportunities to strengthen skills such as:

  • Policy research;
  • Report writing;
  • Analytical writing;
  • Project management;
  • Financial analysis;
  • Communications;
  • Stakeholder engagement;
  • Event management;
  • Administrative coordination; and
  • International teamwork.

3. Multinational Working Environment

Interns work in an institution involving professionals from different national, cultural and professional backgrounds.

This exposure can be particularly valuable to students and graduates interested in international organizations, diplomacy, development, environmental policy or multilateral cooperation.

4. Professional Mentorship and Learning

Participants may work alongside experienced OSCE professionals, creating opportunities to learn from colleagues with expertise across policy, programme management, administration and international affairs.

5. Professional Networking

The programme also gives interns opportunities to meet other young professionals with similar interests and establish professional connections within an international environment.

Internship Duration

Successful applicants may be appointed for periods ranging from two to six months.

The precise starting date will depend on the operational requirements of the relevant hiring office.

Applicants should also understand that the maximum cumulative internship period with the OSCE is six months.

This means that an individual who has already completed six months of internship service with the OSCE cannot subsequently undertake another OSCE internship, even if the second position is located at another duty station.

Full-Time Working Arrangement

OSCE internships are normally undertaken on a full-time basis of approximately 40 hours per week.

However, the vacancy indicates that flexible arrangements involving part-time internships may be approved in special circumstances.

Applicants should therefore generally prepare for full-time participation unless an alternative arrangement is specifically agreed with the OSCE.

Tasks and Responsibilities of OSCE Economic and Environmental Interns

Interns may be assigned a broad range of responsibilities depending on the department, programme and operational needs of the OSCE Secretariat.

The vacancy provides examples of the assignments interns may undertake.

1. Research and Policy Writing

A significant portion of an intern’s work may involve research and drafting.

Assignments can include preparation of:

  • Research papers;
  • Policy reports;
  • Concept papers;
  • Briefing papers;
  • Internal memoranda;
  • Talking points;
  • Speeches;
  • Background documents;
  • Newsletters;
  • Presentations; and
  • Other policy or programme materials.

This aspect of the internship makes strong analytical, research and writing skills particularly valuable.

2. Project Management and Implementation

Interns may assist with the design, management and implementation of OSCE projects.

Possible tasks include:

  • Supporting preparation of project proposals;
  • Assisting with project budgets;
  • Monitoring project implementation;
  • Compiling information from project activities; and
  • Preparing progress reports for donors.

This can provide practical experience with the project cycle used by international organizations and donor-supported programmes.

3. Thematic Research and Analysis

Interns may conduct research on subjects relevant to OSCE activities.

Depending on the assignment, this could include:

  • Thematic policy research;
  • Legal research;
  • Assisting with reviews of legal documents;
  • Supporting preparation of legal opinions;
  • Media monitoring;
  • Surveys;
  • Financial analysis; and
  • Compilation and interpretation of data.

Candidates with strong research and analytical capabilities may therefore find the internship especially relevant.

4. Communications and Outreach

Some interns may support communications-related activities.

Possible responsibilities include:

  • Updating websites;
  • Preparing publications;
  • Developing booklets;
  • Producing leaflets;
  • Supporting outreach campaigns; and
  • Producing audio-visual material for social media.

This creates opportunities for candidates with communications and digital-content capabilities alongside their substantive academic background.

5. Event and Conference Support

The OSCE regularly organizes meetings and international events.

Interns may help organize:

  • Meetings;
  • Regional workshops;
  • Press conferences;
  • Round-table discussions;
  • Conferences; and
  • Other professional events.

Responsibilities can range from preparing background materials to logistical and administrative coordination.

6. Participation in OSCE Meetings

Depending on their placement, interns may attend meetings involving OSCE decision-making or related bodies.

Tasks may include:

  • Taking minutes;
  • Preparing meeting summaries;
  • Drafting official records;
  • Writing reports; and
  • Supporting follow-up activities.

This can provide valuable exposure to multilateral decision-making processes.

7. Administrative and Operational Support

Internships are not limited to substantive policy work.

Participants may also support operational departments responsible for areas such as:

  • Human resources;
  • Financial services;
  • Procurement;
  • Supply-chain activities;
  • Travel management;
  • Information technology;
  • Communications technology; and
  • General administration.

These responsibilities can help participants understand how a major international institution functions beyond its visible policy activities.

8. Supporting Senior Management

Interns can also assist senior managers in preparing for:

  • Official travel;
  • Bilateral meetings;
  • Country visits;
  • External meetings; and
  • Other engagements.

This may involve preparing briefing packages, compiling background materials, supporting logistical arrangements and communicating with internal and external stakeholders.

Educational Requirements

Applicants are expected to meet the OSCE’s academic requirements.

Candidates should have either:

  • Completed at least two years of full-time post-secondary education; or
  • Graduated from an eligible academic programme within two years before the application deadline.

The applicant’s educational background should be relevant to the work of the internship.

Fields specifically identified by the OSCE include:

  • Economics;
  • Environmental science;
  • Development studies;
  • International development;
  • Finance; or
  • Other comparable fields.

Applicants studying closely related areas may also be suitable where their academic background aligns with the internship’s economic and environmental work.

Age Requirement

Candidates must not be older than 30 years of age on December 31, 2026, which is the closing date of the vacancy.

Applicants should assess their eligibility according to their age on the official deadline rather than their age on the day they submit the application.

English-Language Requirement

Applicants are expected to have professional fluency in English, both written and spoken.

They should be able to communicate information clearly and concisely.

Candidates should also be prepared to demonstrate their communication capabilities during the recruitment process because interviews may form part of the selection procedure.

Other Skills and Competencies Required

In addition to academic qualifications, the OSCE is looking for candidates demonstrating strong personal and professional capabilities.

Applicants should possess:

  • High motivation;
  • Open-mindedness;
  • Flexibility;
  • Ability to work collaboratively;
  • Capacity to build effective professional relationships;
  • Ability to work with individuals from different national, cultural and religious backgrounds;
  • Impartiality;
  • Objectivity;
  • Awareness of gender considerations in professional work; and
  • Computer literacy.

Candidates should be familiar with standard Microsoft Office applications, particularly:

  • Microsoft Excel;
  • Microsoft PowerPoint;
  • Word-processing software; and
  • Email applications.

Additional Experience That Can Strengthen an Application

Certain qualifications are considered assets rather than mandatory requirements.

These include:

Relevant Work Experience

Previous professional, volunteer, research or internship experience connected with economics, environmental affairs, development, finance or international organizations can strengthen a candidate’s profile.

Multicultural or Multilateral Experience

Experience working in an international, multicultural or multilateral environment is advantageous.

Organizational Skills

Candidates who can manage multiple assignments simultaneously and maintain attention to deadlines may have a stronger profile.

Analytical and Research Skills

Research, analytical reasoning and the ability to translate information into well-structured written outputs are useful for many of the assignments associated with the internship.

Drafting Skills

Strong professional writing skills are valuable because interns may contribute to reports, briefings, concept notes, presentations and policy documents.

Additional OSCE-Region Language

Knowledge of another language spoken within the OSCE region is regarded as an advantage, although professional English remains the central language requirement identified in the vacancy.

Internship Locations: Vienna and Prague

The primary duty location listed for this internship is the OSCE Secretariat in Vienna, Austria.

The vacancy also identifies Prague, Czechia, as an additional potential location.

The actual placement of a successful applicant will depend on the hiring office and organizational requirements.

Is the OSCE Internship Paid?

Applicants should understand the funding conditions carefully.

The OSCE states that its internships do not provide a salary or remuneration, and the organization does not reimburse an intern’s travel expenses associated with relocation to or from the duty station.

However, the receiving OSCE office is expected to contribute toward the cost of living for eligible international and national interns who are non-residents of the duty station.

If a receiving office is unable to provide such a cost-of-living contribution, it may instead accept interns who are already residents of the duty station.

Applicants should therefore not describe this programme as a salaried internship and should consider accommodation, travel and personal financial requirements carefully before accepting an offer.

Insurance Arrangements

Selected interns must have health insurance that is valid at their assigned duty station.

If an intern does not already possess appropriate health coverage, the individual may participate in the relevant group health-insurance scheme at their own expense.

The OSCE, however, provides life and disability insurance for interns under the conditions described in the vacancy.

Visa Support

Some selected candidates may require a D visa or another appropriate authorization to undertake the internship at the OSCE Secretariat.

Where such documentation is required, the OSCE indicates that it can support the selected intern by providing an appropriate support letter.

Candidates remain responsible for ensuring they comply with applicable immigration and entry requirements.

Does the Internship Lead to Employment?

No guarantee of future employment is attached to the internship.

The OSCE explicitly states that participation in an internship lasting two to six months does not constitute a commitment to future employment with the organization.

Candidates should therefore view the programme primarily as a professional-learning and practical-experience opportunity.

How to Apply for the OSCE Economic and Environmental Dimension Internship

Candidates who meet the eligibility requirements must submit their application through the official OSCE online recruitment system.

Applicants should carefully complete all information requested through the application platform.

Importantly, the vacancy specifically asks candidates to mention their availability dates in their cover letter.

An effective application should therefore clearly indicate:

  1. The applicant’s earliest available starting date;
  2. The period during which they can undertake the internship;
  3. Their academic background;
  4. Their interest in the Economic and Environmental Dimension;
  5. Relevant research, analytical, policy, environmental, economic or project experience;
  6. Relevant language and technical skills; and
  7. How the internship fits their academic or early-career objectives.

Applications should be submitted through the official OSCE vacancy page before the deadline.

Selection Process

Submission of an application does not guarantee an interview.

The OSCE states that only candidates selected to proceed to subsequent stages of the recruitment process will be contacted.

Applicants should therefore make sure their application clearly demonstrates how they meet the essential criteria rather than relying on generic statements about their interest in international organizations.

Diversity and Inclusion at the OSCE

The OSCE states that it is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Qualified women and men from different:

  • Religious backgrounds;
  • Ethnic backgrounds; and
  • Social backgrounds

are encouraged to apply, provided they satisfy the nationality and other eligibility criteria.

Successful candidates are also expected to maintain the standards required of international civil servants, including professionalism, integrity, independence, impartiality and appropriate ethical conduct.

Important Warning About Application Fees

Applicants should be alert to recruitment scams.

The OSCE explicitly states that it does not request payment at any stage of the application or review process.

Any request demanding money in exchange for submitting, reviewing or progressing an OSCE internship application should therefore be treated with caution.

Application Deadline

The official closing date for the OSCE Internship – Economic and Environmental Dimension is:

December 31, 2026

The vacancy was originally issued on July 3, 2026 and lists multiple available internship posts.

Why This OSCE Internship Is Worth Considering

For young professionals seeking careers in international development, environmental governance, economics, sustainability, multilateral organizations or international public policy, this internship provides exposure to the way economic and environmental questions are addressed within a comprehensive international-security framework.

The breadth of possible assignments is particularly valuable. An intern could potentially contribute to policy research on one project, assist with donor reporting on another, participate in an international meeting and support communications or administrative work.

This combination gives participants an opportunity to understand not only the subject matter of international organizations but also the institutional processes behind their work.

The programme may be especially useful for students and recent graduates interested in future careers with:

  • International organizations;
  • Government institutions;
  • Development agencies;
  • Environmental organizations;
  • Research institutions;
  • International NGOs;
  • Multilateral development organizations;
  • Public-policy organizations;
  • International financial institutions; or
  • Diplomatic and foreign-policy institutions.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Applicants should avoid submitting a generic cover letter that simply states an interest in the OSCE.

A stronger application should connect the candidate’s academic and practical experience directly to the vacancy.

Consider emphasizing:

  • Relevant university coursework;
  • Research projects;
  • Academic papers;
  • Sustainability or environmental projects;
  • Economic or financial analysis;
  • Project-management experience;
  • Policy-writing experience;
  • International-development exposure;
  • Volunteer experience;
  • Multicultural teamwork;
  • Data-analysis capabilities;
  • Knowledge of Excel and other Microsoft Office applications;
  • Strong drafting and research abilities; and
  • A clear understanding of the relationship between economic, environmental and security issues.

Candidates should also explicitly state their availability dates, as requested by the OSCE.

Conclusion

The OSCE Economic and Environmental Dimension Internship 2026 offers students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain practical professional experience within one of the world’s leading regional security organizations.

With placements potentially available in Vienna and Prague, successful candidates can gain exposure to economic governance, environmental security, sustainable development, anti-corruption, natural-resource management, research, programme implementation, communications and international institutional operations.

The programme is particularly relevant to candidates studying or recently graduated in economics, environmental science, development studies, international development, finance or related disciplines.

Internships last between two and six months, with multiple positions available. Although the programme is not salaried and travel expenses are not reimbursed, eligible non-resident interns may receive a contribution toward living costs from the receiving office under the conditions set by the OSCE.

Applicants must meet the academic, age, language and nationality requirements and should submit a carefully prepared application through the official OSCE recruitment system.

The application deadline is December 31, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), Bureau of International Labor Affairs (ILAB) has announced the Fostering the Future Together: Empowering Youth for a Safe Digital World funding opportunity, supporting projects that promote child well-being, online safety, positive youth development, education, digital skills, and protection from child labor and online exploitation.

The funding opportunity, FOA-ILAB-26-43, provides approximately $15 million in total funding through cooperative agreements. Up to five organizations are expected to receive awards ranging from $2 million to $3 million each.

This is an organization-focused funding opportunity rather than an individual grant. Eligible organizations from the United States and other countries may apply, provided they satisfy the detailed requirements in the official Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA).

Opportunity Overview

Opportunity Fostering the Future Together: Empowering Youth for a Safe Digital World
Funding opportunity number FOA-ILAB-26-43
Agency U.S. Department of Labor
Bureau Bureau of International Labor Affairs
Assistance Listing 17.401 – International Labor Programs
Funding instrument Cooperative Agreement
Total funding Approximately $15 million
Expected awards 5
Award amount $2 million–$3 million
Cost sharing Not required
Deadline September 10, 2026
Application deadline time 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
Project duration Up to 27 months
Application platform Grants.gov
Opportunity type Discretionary

The opportunity was posted on August 11, 2026, and the current announcement lists September 10, 2026 as the closing date.

What Is the Fostering the Future Together Grant?

The Fostering the Future Together (FTFT) initiative is designed to support international projects addressing challenges affecting children and young people in the digital era.

The U.S. Department of Labor’s Bureau of International Labor Affairs is making approximately $15 million available for five cooperative agreements. The projects are intended to support the FTFT global coalition’s goals related to:

  • Child well-being
  • Online child protection
  • Positive youth development
  • Prevention of child labor
  • Prevention of online exploitation
  • Access to quality education
  • Digital skills development
  • Safe pathways into employment
  • Apprenticeships and skills training
  • Strengthening government capacity
  • Collaboration with the private sector

The full FOA indicates that projects are expected to operate internationally and complement or build upon relevant country commitments under the Fostering the Future Together global coalition.

What Will the Funding Support?

The funding is intended for projects that address interconnected challenges facing children and youth, particularly the risks associated with digital technologies, child labor, exploitation, education, and transitions into employment.

According to the FOA, proposed projects should focus on several major areas.

1. Expanding Access to Quality Education

Organizations may develop projects designed to connect children who are at risk of or have withdrawn from education with quality education opportunities and technology-enabled learning.

The objective is to help vulnerable children access educational opportunities that can support their development and future prospects.

Projects should consider the specific circumstances of the country where they will operate and demonstrate how proposed activities respond to local needs.

2. Connecting Youth With Skills and Apprenticeships

Another major focus is connecting young people of legal working age with safe, market-relevant apprenticeship and skills-training opportunities.

The program particularly emphasizes:

  • Digital skills
  • Workforce preparation
  • Apprenticeships
  • Dignified employment
  • Market-relevant training
  • Technology-enabled learning
  • Introduction of America EdTech tools and training

The objective is to help young people develop skills that can improve their employment prospects while ensuring that pathways into work are safe and appropriate.

3. Protecting Children From Online Exploitation

The opportunity also focuses heavily on online safety.

Funded projects may develop and implement:

  • Child-centered online safety protocols
  • Online safety tools
  • Training modules
  • Educational resources
  • Awareness initiatives
  • Protection mechanisms

These interventions are expected to address risks including online exploitation, predatory practices, and the recruitment or involvement of children in harmful labor activities through digital platforms.

The FOA specifically highlights the importance of developing resources for educators, parents, and children.

4. Strengthening Government Capacity

The program recognizes that preventing child labor and online exploitation requires strong national and local institutions.

Projects may therefore work with governments to strengthen their capacity to:

  • Prevent online exploitation
  • Enforce child labor laws
  • Respond to emerging digital threats
  • Protect children and young people
  • Improve relevant systems and policies

This makes government engagement an important component for organizations developing their project proposals.

5. Working With the Private Sector

The funding opportunity also encourages partnerships with private-sector stakeholders.

These partnerships can help develop sustainable, market-driven solutions addressing child labor and online exploitation risks.

Applicants should therefore consider whether businesses, technology companies, educational organizations, employers, or other private-sector actors can contribute meaningfully to their proposed intervention.

Learn More Here

Where Will Projects Be Implemented?

The funding is intended for international implementation.

The FOA states that up to $15 million will support projects implemented in five countries, with at least one project in each of the following regions:

  • Africa
  • Asia
  • Latin America and the Caribbean

The project must comply with the FOA’s country eligibility and geographic requirements. Applicants should therefore consult the full announcement carefully before selecting a proposed implementation country.

This means that organizations should not assume that every country worldwide is automatically eligible.

The geographic focus must correspond with the countries and requirements specified in the official FOA.

Who Can Apply?

The funding opportunity is designed for organizations rather than individual applicants.

The eligibility information published by Simpler.Grants.gov states that eligible applicants may include:

  • Commercial organizations
  • International organizations
  • Educational institutions
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Faith-based organizations
  • Community-based organizations
  • Public international organizations (PIOs)

Faith-based organizations are specifically encouraged to apply.

The Department of Labor also states that it will not discriminate in the selection or administration of awards based on an organization’s religious character, affiliation, exercise, or lack thereof, where the organization is otherwise similarly situated to eligible secular organizations.

Important Eligibility Point

Although the public eligibility summary identifies broad categories of organizations, applicants must satisfy all applicable requirements in the full FOA, including country, project, partnership, and technical requirements.

Organizations should therefore not rely solely on the short eligibility summary when determining whether they qualify.

International and U.S. Organizations Can Apply

The eligibility structure is broader than many U.S.-only government funding opportunities.

The published eligibility information includes international organizations and non-U.S. organizations, in addition to U.S.-based entities.

Therefore, eligible organizations from Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, the United States, and other relevant locations may potentially participate, subject to the specific country and project requirements of the FOA.

This is particularly significant for organizations already working on:

  • Child protection
  • Digital safety
  • Youth development
  • Education
  • Child labor prevention

Why This Opportunity Matters

The digital transformation of society has created significant opportunities for children and young people, but it has also introduced new forms of vulnerability.

Children can encounter exploitation, predatory behavior, harmful content, recruitment into labor, and other risks through online platforms.

At the same time, young people need relevant skills to participate successfully in modern labor markets.

The Fostering the Future Together opportunity attempts to address these challenges through an integrated approach combining:

  1. Education;
  2. Digital safety;
  3. Child protection;
  4. Skills development;
  5. Apprenticeships;
  6. Government capacity;
  7. Private-sector collaboration; and
  8. Prevention of child labor and exploitation.

This makes the opportunity potentially relevant to organizations working across multiple sectors rather than only traditional labor-focused organizations.
